sections.description: Right-click works in Media Studio: the menu opens at the pointer in every view. Update installs use the approved non-blocking pill and decision ledger, and Theme Styles edge controls stay inside their card.
sections.changelog:
v1.3.538 — The launcher stacks in a column with the ACSS icon

  • MV sat above the Automatic.css icon but 6.5px out of line with it. The launcher now takes the detected dock’s own centre, so the two read as a column. With no dock present it returns to its normal offset.

v1.3.537 — The dock scan stopped before it reached the dock

  • The scan capped itself at 4000 nodes. A builder page is far larger, and a plugin’s dock is appended near the end of body — so it gave up before reaching it. Reproduced in a real browser: old scan 16px, new scan 57px in one read. The cap is gone and the scan now reads from the end backwards.

v1.3.536 — MV finally floats above the ACSS icon

  • A MutationObserver on the document cannot see a shadow root being filled, which is why the previous attempt missed the Automatic.css icon. Replaced with a bounded poll that stops as soon as it finds a dock.

v1.3.535 — Reload the builder is never a silent no-op

  • Cancelling Bricks’ unsaved-changes prompt used to leave the button dead on the second press. It now retries out of the click frame, then as a plain navigation, and if the browser still refuses it says so and names Ctrl+R.

v1.3.534 — Enter edits a chip, and a late dock is still found

  • Enter on a token chip opens it for editing instead of failing with “Type at least one attribute.” — there was no keyboard route into edit mode before.
  • MV now watches for a floating dock that mounts after it does, which is why the Automatic.css icon was being missed: its dashboard attaches its shadow root late.

v1.3.533 — Pasted classes, the ACSS icon, and one centre line

  • Pasting class="name" into the bar now adds the class instead of trying to set a class attribute. Several classes at once work too.
  • MV’s launcher clears the Automatic.css icon. The earlier attempt measured nothing because ACSS puts its launcher inside an open shadow root, which querySelectorAll does not pierce.
  • The update pill and the launcher share one horizontal centre line.

v1.3.532 — Reload the builder works

  • Reload the builder and Later did nothing: a pointerdown on the update dock counted as clicking outside a panel, so the capture-phase handler closed the open studio and unmounted both buttons before the click landed. The dock is exempt now, as the toasts and the media frame already were.

v1.3.531 — The floating docks stop colliding

  • The update pill moved clear of the launcher, which it used to sit on top of while an update was pending.
  • MV’s launcher now steps above another plugin’s dock — Automatic.css parks one in the same corner — by measuring what is there rather than matching a vendor class.

v1.3.530 — Enter applies a suggestion in Mimam’s Bar

  • Enter on an autocomplete suggestion filled the input and stopped; the Apply button was the only way to finish. Tab now completes, Enter completes and applies — except where the suggestion leaves a placeholder to fill.

v1.3.529 — The outlines actually go this time

  • v1.3.528 named five classes and reached almost nothing. Replaced with a default plus an explicit keep-list: everything in the studio loses its border except spinners, check boxes, swatches, the drop zone, table rules, artwork, focus rings and accent states. Fields take a fill instead.

v1.3.528 — Media Studio matches the calm mock

  • Tiles now rise out of the grid instead of sinking into it, the shell and panels sit at the right level, body text is #dedede, fields are fills rather than outlines, and the 633 decorative borders are gone — while spinners, check boxes and focus rings keep theirs.

v1.3.527 — Media Studio uses its type ramp

  • The studio was rendering one size and one weight for everything, so no 13px titles or 10px meta labels showed. The blanket rule’s :not() chain outranked the exceptions it was written to yield to; the exclusions moved into :where(), which costs no specificity.

v1.3.526 — The grid columns fill the width

  • The tracks were sizing to their content instead of to 1fr, leaving 74px parked against the right edge. Re-declared the template at studio scope so it wins.

v1.3.525 — The grid fills the width on All media

  • Fixed the empty strip down the right of the grid: the middle column had no flex-grow, so the width the details panel would have used was left blank instead of going to the tiles.

v1.3.524 — Reverted to the last good Media Studio

  • This is v1.3.516’s code shipped forward. Everything structural from v1.3.517 to v1.3.523 is reverted — the CSS extraction, the lazy studio split, the masonry change and the type-ramp change. Media Studio returns to the state it was in before that work.
  • Kept: the right-click menu, the release webhook and the conditional update check. Lost: the admin-page weight reduction — every admin page parses the full bundle again.

v1.3.523 — The type ramp was never actually applying

  • The studio has rendered one size and one weight since v1.3.511. The blanket rule used a :not() chain whose specificity outranked the 13px and 10px exceptions it was written to yield to, so the naming-back never applied to anything. The exclusions moved into :where(), which costs no specificity.

v1.3.522 — Masonry staggers again

  • Masonry had been rendering as a plain grid with images clipped to a repeating pattern. Five :nth-child rules faked a stagger from a time when tiles were direct siblings; they now count position within a column, so every column got the same heights. Removed — tile size comes from the file’s own aspect ratio.

v1.3.521 — The code editor is styled again, and studios open without a wait

  • Fixed the Stylesheet and code editors, broken in v1.3.517: the panel stylesheet was enqueued before CodeMirror's and lost 9 rules that carry no !important. It now loads last, as it always effectively did.
  • The studio bundle is fetched during idle time after the page settles, not on first click, so opening a studio no longer waits on the network.

v1.3.520 — The launcher is back

  • Fixes v1.3.519, which made the plugin unreachable. The helpers object the panel hands to the studios listed a name that does not exist at the top level, so building it threw and took the whole panel with it — no launcher, no studios, no way in.
  • Added a check that executes builder-panel.js against a stub DOM and fails if it throws. Every text-based check passed on the broken build; none of them can see a ReferenceError.

v1.3.519 — The studios load when you open one

  • Content Studio, Media Studio, Font Manager and Plugin Studio — 538 KB — are fetched the first time one is opened. With v1.3.517 that takes what every wp-admin page parses from 1784 KB to 712 KB, a 60% cut.
  • The launcher prefetches on hover, so the code is usually there before you click. A studio that fails to load says so and offers to retry.

v1.3.518 — Asking whether there is an update stops costing 260 KB

  • The update check is now a conditional request. An unchanged feed answers 304 with an empty body instead of re-sending the ~260 KB manifest, so the Dev cache falls to 60 seconds and a new build is picked up within a minute with no per-site configuration.
  • The stored copy and its validator outlive the freshness window, so a 304 has something to hand back; both are cleared by Check update.

v1.3.517 — The stylesheet stops being JavaScript

  • Moved 560 KB of CSS out of builder-panel.js into assets/css/panel.css. Every wp-admin page had been downloading and parsing it as script before any of it could be applied. The bundle drops from 1784 KB to 1244 KB — a 30% cut on every admin page, whether or not MV is opened.
  • Enqueued after MV's other stylesheets so it keeps the cascade position it had when it was injected at DOMContentLoaded.

v1.3.516 — Updates arrive when they are published

  • Added a release webhook. GitHub POSTs on push, the site clears its update cache and re-reads the manifest within seconds. Polling could only shorten the gap; this closes it. The endpoint is guarded by an HMAC-SHA256 signature and is inert until a secret is configured.
  • The manifest cache is now per channel: Dev falls to 5 minutes, Beta and Stable keep 6 hours.
  • Fixed wp-admin keeping MV's layout after MV had let go of it — the Media Library replacement set padding and margin on the admin content column and never restored them.

v1.3.515 — Right-click aims the menu, it does not select

  • Right-clicking a file no longer ticks its checkbox, opens the batch bar or fills the details panel. The tile the menu belongs to carries a dashed ring instead, which is what the approved mock specified all along.
  • Right-clicking inside an existing selection still acts on all of it, so plural labels stay truthful; outside it, the menu acts on that one file and leaves the selection untouched.

v1.3.514 — The right-click menu was throwing, not hiding

  • ctxRows() called collectionLabel(), which has never existed anywhere in the codebase. Building the Add to collection submenu threw a ReferenceError, the Preact render died with it, and the menu never reached the DOM. That is the real reason right-click did nothing, and it was there from the first build. The correct function is collLabel(), three lines away in the same component.
  • It survived five builds because the throw surfaced only as an unhandled promise rejection inside Preact — no error at the point of failure, no element to inspect, and nothing wrong in the source when read line by line.
  • The v1.3.513 positioning work is kept and was a real defect, but it was not what blocked the menu; those notes overstated it and this build corrects the claim.
  • The contract check now resolves every identifier ctxRows calls against a definition, so an invented helper fails the build instead of failing silently at runtime.

v1.3.513 — The right-click menu was never missing, only off screen

  • Fixed the media context menu for real. It has rendered correctly since v1.3.512 — at the coordinates the cursor reported — and was then drawn inside a panel that had quietly become its frame of reference. Media Studio is excluded from the transform reset, so its panel keeps a transform; a transform makes an element the containing block for every fixed-position descendant inside it; and the studio clips what leaves its box. A menu placed at x 1180 landed 1180px inside an 880px panel and was cut away.
  • It worked in fullscreen the whole time, because fullscreen sets transform to none. That is what made four builds read as intermittent rather than wrong, and why reading the source kept saying the fix was already in.
  • The menu is now positioned against the studio box, which is the frame the collection menu has always used and the one thing in this area that never broke. Flip, clamp and the submenu all measure in that same frame.
  • Right-click now answers only in the studio it belongs to. MediaStudioSub is mounted more than once — the Content Studio picker and the standalone panel — and a listener on document meant one click opened a menu in each.
  • Added scripts/check-v1-3-513-context-menu.js, which fails on every one of the ten ways this has already broken.

v1.3.512 — Right-click actually reaches Media Studio

  • Fixed the media context menu never opening. The listener sat on document in the bubble phase, and Media Studio’s own collection menus — plus several WP-admin and Bricks handlers — call stopPropagation on contextmenu, so it was being silenced before it was ever reached. It now listens in the capture phase, which runs on the way down before anything can stop it.
  • Guarded the target as well: a right-click can land on a text node or the document, where closest() does not exist. That threw inside the listener and killed it silently for the rest of the session.

v1.3.511 — The Media Studio type ramp, in one sweep

  • Replaced four builds of per-class type fixes with a single rule. Most of what was still off the ramp reported no class at all, so no targeted selector could ever reach it — chasing them one at a time could not finish.
  • Rule 4 is a default with exceptions, so it is written that way now: everything in the studio takes 11.5px at 400, then 13px is named back for titles and the overview numbers, 10px for meta, and 600 for emphasis and for what is on.
  • Icons are excluded by name rather than left to luck. A glyph is artwork standing in for a control and needs its pixel size — 10, 14, 15 and 18 are all deliberate — and rule 0 warns that a blanket sweep is unsafe wherever the thing being swept is sometimes load-bearing.

v1.3.510 — The last of the Media Studio type ramp

  • Closed out the type ramp using a computed-style sweep of the running panel rather than the stylesheet. Reading the source had said the pass was finished twice; the render disagreed both times. Remaining sizes were 9, 10.5, 11, 12 and 14 at weights 400, 600, 650, 700 and 800.
  • COLLECTIONS and the remaining uppercase labels are sentence case. The MV collection badge keeps its capitals — it is an acronym, which rule 5 exempts — but comes off 9px/650 and loses its letter-spacing.
  • Inputs, menu buttons, small buttons, the list preview, the dropzone and the sidebar actions all move onto 11.5px. A blanket text-transform and letter-spacing reset covers the labels that carry no class of their own and so could not be reached any other way.

v1.3.509 — Collection details no longer pushed outside the modal

  • Fixed the Collection details panel being clipped by the right edge of Media Studio. Measured in the live studio, the layout ran to 2039px against a modal edge at about 1789 — 250px of the third column outside the window.
  • The middle column was already able to shrink (min-width 0, overflow hidden) but the layout around it was not: a grid child defaults to min-width auto and refuses to go below its content width, so the overflow was pushed onto the last column instead of being absorbed by the middle one. The layout is now guarded, which is what lets the file list give up width when details opens.

v1.3.508 — List view headers and the alt-text field

  • Styled the three list header cells the pass had missed. Only .ve-list-meta had been targeted, so PREVIEW, FILENAME and ALT TEXT (AUTO-SAVES ON BLUR) stayed 9px/800/uppercase sitting beside sentence-case neighbours in the same row.
  • The inline alt-text field in list view is a field rather than a pill: it takes a fill instead of an outline, and the accent only on focus.

v1.3.507 — Media Studio: the rest of the calm pass

  • Completed the Media Studio pass across the surfaces v1.3.506 did not reach: masonry cards, the collection-details panel and its status cards, the filter builder and saved filters, the list column chooser, collection chips and the empty state. All of these already existed; what was missing was the pass reaching them, so the shell had moved while they had not.
  • Collection details keeps its accent because the hero marks a state, but the fill stops shouting and its status cards recess into the panel holding them rather than sitting outlined on it.
  • Filter pills, choices and the search field lose their outlines for fills; the active choice takes the accent, which is the one thing in that row that means state.
  • The empty state is no longer the dimmest thing on screen — it is the one place with nothing else to look at.

v1.3.506 — Media Studio shell to the UI rules

  • Media Studio’s shell now follows docs/UI-RULES.md, completing what v1.3.503 started on the tiles and metadata cards. The rail and details panel sit at panel level while the grid recesses to a well beneath them, so the studio has a floor and things standing on it rather than one flat plane.
  • Overview cards rise out of the grid instead of sinking into it. They were dropping 0.9 L* while the tiles beside them rose 10.2 — the same container moving two directions at once, which is what made that band read flat.
  • Cut the shell to three type sizes at two weights, and replaced the uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels (Collections, Total media, Alt text, Metadata, Shortcode) with sentence case.
  • Lifted the dim text colours, which measured 2.8–3.8 against a 4.5 contrast floor. Filter and column popovers now step above the panel they float over instead of matching its tone.

v1.3.505 — The update dock speaks the surface it is on

  • The update dock no longer says “Reload the builder” in wp-admin, where there is no builder. Five strings now follow the surface: the button reads Reload the page, and the ledger says this page rather than the builder is running the previous files.

v1.3.504 — Update scrim, and right-click in every Media Studio view

  • The update ledger now dims and blurs the page behind it once an install has finished or failed, so the decision it is asking for stops competing with everything else. A running install still leaves the page usable, which is the whole point of the corner pill.
  • Right-click now works in all three Media Studio views. The menu was attached to the grid containers, so the list table — rendered by a different function — never answered. The listener now sits on the document while the studio is mounted, and list rows carry their id.

v1.3.503 — Media Studio right-click, and the calm pass

  • Right-click a file in Media Studio. Twelve rows reaching every per-item action MV has: open in the panel or the WP editor, copy the URL, copy as file path or HTML tag, insert into a Bricks control, replace, convert, add to or remove from a collection, download, delete.
  • The primary verb stays flat and its variants fold — Copy URL is visible with File path and HTML tag behind Copy as, and Convert to holds the three formats. Nothing is reachable only by guessing.
  • Right-clicking outside the selection takes it over; right-clicking inside keeps it, so a plural label is always truthful. Delete keeps its confirmation dialog. Text fields keep the browser’s own menu, where Paste and spellcheck live.
  • The menu flips rather than clips near a viewport edge, and caps its height so the full list stays reachable in a short builder window.
  • Media Studio now follows the MV UI rules: tile outlines became lifts so depth comes from lightness, cards recess inside the panels holding them, and the type came down from six sizes and weights up to 900 to three sizes at 400 and 600.

v1.3.502 — One shortcut registry and a Shortcuts settings page

  • Every rebindable key now comes from one registry (assets/js/shortcut-registry.js) instead of being decided inline where it fires. Settings → Shortcuts lists all thirteen, each with its keys, scope and on/off switch on one line.
  • Click a shortcut’s keys and press what you want. Chords take a single letter, modifier shortcuts take the combination you hold. The leader key and the chord window are editable, and one button restores every default.
  • Chords are now a single state machine rather than a timestamp field per shortcut. R R renames and U U unlinks as before; ? ? opens a cheat sheet; G plus a letter opens a panel and ships off, so a new install claims no letter you did not ask for.
  • Enabling a chord claims its letter: the lone press is swallowed so Bricks cannot act on it. Letters Bricks already uses are marked amber on the settings page while you choose, rather than being blocked outright.
  • An armed chord shows a chip at the bottom of the screen naming the key it is waiting for. After the leader, a letter bound to nothing is shown as rejected; a lone letter that leads nowhere is simply forgotten.
  • Each shortcut carries its own Builder / Admin / Both scope, so the selection chords stay in the builder while the panel ones can work in wp-admin.

v1.3.501 — Upload failure toast dismissal

  • Dismissing a failed upload no longer depends on CSS :has(). The failure toast stops auto-hiding so its reason can be read, so the close button has to work everywhere the builder runs.

v1.3.500 — Update dock visual pass and Media Studio font uploads

  • Rebuilt the update install dock to the approved Variant D visual pass. Depth now comes from surface lightness rather than outlines, so the pill and ledger sit above the builder canvas instead of reading flat against it, and the release-notes block recesses inside the ledger holding it.
  • Reduced the dock to the MV type ramp: three sizes (13/11.5/10) and two weights (400/600), replacing seven sizes and weights up to 900. The only edges left are the eight step dots, where the border is the control.
  • Moved success and failure signalling onto the progress ring alone, so the accent marks state and nothing else. Renamed the final install stage from “Refreshing update caches” to “Finishing up”.
  • Allowed font files (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF, OTF) to be uploaded through Media Studio. WordPress permits no font type in the media library, so every font dropped on a Fonts collection was rejected before it could become an attachment. Scoped to Media Studio uploads by a user who may already upload files, and every file is checked against its format signature.
  • Made a failed upload state its reason. The toast reported “0 uploaded · 2 failed” and discarded the message WordPress had returned, leaving the cause invisible; it now shows the reason and stays until dismissed.

Older notes are in the repository CHANGELOG. Trimmed at v1.3.519, where the feed had grown to 344 entries to display five.
